th.aboutTitle: เกี่ยวกับบ้านรอดไหม?
th.aboutIntro: บ้านรอดไหม? ช่วยให้ทุกบ้านพร้อมรับมือทุกภัย: รู้ว่าต้องทำอะไรเมื่อน้ำท่วม น้ำป่า พายุ แผ่นดินไหว ไฟไหม้ ไฟดับ อากาศร้อนจัด หรือฝุ่น PM2.5 เช็กของจำเป็นตามจำนวนคนในบ้าน จัดกระเป๋าฉุกเฉิน ทำการ์ดแผนครอบครัวและบัตรข้อมูลฉุกเฉิน ส่งข่าวว่าปลอดภัย คำนวณว่าตอนไฟดับของในตู้เย็นยังกินได้ไหม ดูว่าฝุ่นและความร้อนวันนี้บ้านเราต้องทำอะไร ใส่หน้ากากแบบไหน น้ำดื่มพอกี่วัน ล้างถังพักน้ำใช้คลอรีนเท่าไร พร้อมลิงก์เว็บหน่วยงานรัฐ และมีเกมสั้น 60 วิ ให้จำง่ายกว่าอ่าน (ไม่ต้องเล่นก็ใช้ได้) ทุกคำแนะนำมีที่มา ส่วนใหญ่จากหน่วยงานรัฐไทย (ตรวจสอบเมื่อ ต.ค. 2569) บางข้อมาจากคำแนะนำของต่างประเทศ เช่น องค์การอนามัยโลก หรือ CDC สหรัฐฯ และมีป้ายบอกไว้ ถ้าสถานการณ์จริงต่างออกไป ให้เชื่อประกาศและเจ้าหน้าที่ในพื้นที่ก่อนเสมอ

en.aboutIntro: Baan Rod Mai? helps every home get ready for any disaster: what to do in a flood, flash flood, storm, earthquake, fire, power cut, heatwave or PM2.5 dust; a supplies check and an emergency bag for your household; a family plan card and an emergency info card; a safe message for the family; how long the fridge stays safe in a power cut, what today's dust and heat mean at home, which mask, how long your water lasts and how much chlorine a water tank needs; links to Thai agencies' own pages; and a 60-second game that makes it easier to remember than reading (you don't have to play to use the rest). Every tip has a source, mostly Thai government agencies (checked Oct 2026); some come from international guidance such as WHO or the US CDC and are marked as such. If local announcements say otherwise, follow your local officials.
en.aboutPrivacy: No sign-up, no personal data, no cookies. Scores, what you answer in the tools (supplies check, fridge, dust today) and your family plan card's text stay on your device and are never sent anywhere. We only count plays and shares anonymously (Cloudflare Web Analytics is cookieless), in line with Thailand's PDPA.

en.llmsSummary: Baan Rod Mai? ("Will the house survive?") is a free Thai home-preparedness app for phones, with an English toggle. It is a tool first: short "what to do" guides for nine situations (a flood coming, after a flood, flash floods and landslides, storms and lightning, earthquakes, house fire, power cuts, extreme heat, PM2.5 dust), a supplies check sized to the household and an emergency bag list, a family plan card and an emergency info card (medicines, allergies, contacts), a ready-made "I'm safe" message for LINE or SMS, and calculators that work out what to do from the household's answers (food in the fridge in a power cut, from US agencies' charts; what today's PM2.5 colour means for everyone and for people at risk, from the Pollution Control Department's 2023 bands; which mask for dust, smoke, a flood clean-up or illness, never for a child under 2; what the announced heat-index level means, from the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and the Department of Health; how many days the drinking water lasts; how much chlorine a flooded water tank needs, from the Metropolitan Waterworks Authority and the Department of Disease Control; how many days daily medicine lasts), with links to the agencies' own pages (LINE ALERT, warnings, river levels, planned power cuts, relief) and how to turn on emergency alerts; the owner can put one guide on top of the start screen while it is in the news. A 60-second game is the optional way to learn it: five modes ("Before the flood", "After the water recedes", "PM2.5 dust", "House fire", "Power cut") where players tap the risks in an illustrated house and pick the safe action. Every correct action and every guide line is linked to its source: most come from Thai government agencies (often as quoted in Thai news), some from international guidance only (US CDC, Ready.gov, WHO, Tokyo Metropolitan Government), marked as under review. No sign-up, no cookies, no personal data; what people answer or type in the tools stays on their device.

en.fridgePageTitle: Power cut: what in the fridge to throw out, and what to keep · Baan Rod Mai?
en.fridgePageDesc: In a power cut a closed fridge keeps food safe for about 4 hours; after that, throw out meat, eggs, milk, cooked rice and leftovers, and keep whole fruit and vegetables, bread and sauces. A full freezer keeps about 48 hours, a half-full one about 24, and insulin keeps out of the fridge for up to 28 days, say US agencies. Free.

en.maskPageDesc: On orange dust days everyone wears a mask outdoors, on yellow days the people at risk; choose an N95 first, older people, pregnant women and people with a long-term illness may use a surgical mask instead, and children under 2 wear none. Mould clean-up: an N95. A factory fire nearby: masks can't filter chemical fumes. From Thailand's Department of Health, Department of Disease Control and Pollution Control Department. Free.
